 Coram:
 Justice Chittaranjan Dash
 Order
Heard the learned counsels for the Petitioner and the State.

2. By means of this application, the Petitioner seeks grant of bail U/s.438 Cr.P.C. in apprehension of arrest for his alleged involvement in the offences U/s. 376(2)(n)/417/420/313/506/323/ 379, I.P.C.,
in connection with Pattamundai P.S. Case No.585 of 2022 corresponding to G.R. Case No.585 of 2022 pending in the court of learned J.M.F.C., Pattamundai.
3. Learned counsel for the Petitioner submitted that the Petitioner has been falsely implicated in this case.

According to him, even otherwise if the allegations of the Informant is accepted having regard to the facts and circumstances of the case and the alleged relationship between the Petitioner and the Informant being carried since last 6 to 7 years, the factum of incident as regards rape cannot be said to have been made out to implicate the present Petitioner.

All other narrations in the F.I.R.
being tainted with exaggeration // 2 // cannot be attributed to the present Petitioner, and as such his pre- arrest bail may be considered.
4. Learned counsel for the State on the other hand vehemently opposed the bail application of the Petitioner.

5. Keeping in view the submissions of the parties, on perusal of the F.I.R. as well as the statement of the victim, there are prima facie material which deduce that the Informant had been in relation with the Petitioner since the year 2015.

6. Be that as it may, keeping in view the facts and circumstances of the case, nature of the allegation and the seriousness and gravity of the offence, while this Court is not inclined to grant anticipatory bail, it is directed that, in the event the Petitioner surrenders and moves for bail before the learned J.M.F.C., Pattamundai in the aforesaid G.R. Case within a period of three weeks from today, he shall be allowed to go on bail on such terms and conditions as would be deemed just and proper by the said court, but subject to the following further conditions - (i) The Petitioner shall immediately destroy all the obscene photographs and videos of the Informant kept in his possession in any mode and shall under no circumstance make it public or viral in any social medias / electronic medias in any manner whatsoever.
(ii) Display of such photos / videos of the Informant, if at any point of time in any social media / electronic media would be straightway // 3 // attributable to the present Petitioner having intention to malign the image of the victim informant.
(iii) The Petitioner shall not blackmail, intimidate or harass the Informant under any circumstance on the plea of having the obscene / intimate videos or photographs.

(iv) He shall not antagonize, terrorise or threaten the Informant and her family members as well as the prosecution witnesses and shall not tamper with the prosecution evidence in any manner whatsoever.
(v) He shall appear before the I.O. in person and shall cooperate with the investigation as and when required by the I.O.
(vi) He shall not indulge in any such activities sabotaging or putting the Informant into inconvenience in pursuing her case.
(vii) Violation of any of the conditions shall entail cancellation of bail of the Petitioner.
7.
The ABLAPL is disposed of accordingly.
( Chittaranjan Dash ) Judge S.K. Parida Saroj Kumar Rath vs State Of Odisha ....
